definition.model_description: Run a PowerShell 7 script as the user's Windows account. Only script is required: working_directory defaults to the workspace root and timeout_ms to 120000; give builds, tests and other long commands a larger timeout_ms. The call also ends at the tool time limit in Tool settings (default 10 minutes). Read-only mode asks before running. The script is not sandboxed and can change anything the user can. Set requires_network when it needs the network: read-only and workspace modes then ask for network approval, Full Access allows it, and blocking the network is not enforced. Each call gets a fresh environment and PATH, as in a new terminal, with secret variables removed (filtered_environment_names lists the removed ones your script names). Returns the exit code and stdout and stderr as text; a long stream shows its first 2 KB and last 6 KB, and stdout_next or stderr_next is where shell.query reads the rest. The exit code is that of exit N, or 1 after an uncaught error, else 0 even when a native command failed: end with exit $LASTEXITCODE to report it. Errors name lines of your script. PowerShell quoting is not bash: inside "..." a double quote is `" (\" ends the string) and ` escapes, so JavaScript template literals break; inside '...' double a single quote (''). Put long inline programs (node -e, python -c) in a file with fs.write and run the file. Processes left running stay managed: read them with shell.query and stop them with shell.stop. An interrupted call is never re-run automatically.

definition.model_description: Open an Agent-owned PowerShell 7 or CMD terminal in this session. shell defaults to powershell, working_directory to the workspace root. It runs as the user's Windows account, is not sandboxed, and network blocking is not enforced. Read-only mode asks for run approval; Shell's session run approval also covers terminal.open and terminal.write. requires_network has the same soft network default and approval as Shell. User terminals are never visible. The terminal stays managed until closed; no automatic replay after interruption.

Send input to an Agent terminal in this session; newline submits a line, interrupt sends Ctrl+C first. wait_ms defaults to 2000, up to 30000 and the tool's time limit. until_text returns early when seen. Read-only mode asks for the same run approval as Shell. Returns new plain text with byte offsets; terminal.read pages the retained output. While the user has taken over, model reads and writes are refused; an empty input then waits up to wait_ms for the user to hand it back and returns the terminal's latest output as soon as they do. It is not sandboxed and network blocking is not enforced.

Page the bounded plain UTF-8 output of an Agent terminal in this session. offset defaults to 0, max_bytes to 8192 (1..65536). ANSI/VT controls are removed; truncated output gives a continuation offset and older discarded output is marked. While the user has taken over, wait for them to hand it back before reading. User terminals are never accessible.

Close only the Agent terminal identified in this session and stop its whole managed process tree. Return final status, exit code and bounded plain text. Preserve its output record for this conversation; never stops unrelated user terminals or processes.

Ask the user to type a password or other sensitive text into an Agent-controlled Agent terminal in this session. Supply terminal_id and a clear prompt. Parent Agent only; unavailable to subagents and user terminals. Returns only completed, cancelled or failed, never the input. The user's input is sent directly to the managed terminal and is not recorded or shown to the model. Programs may echo it in the user's live terminal; recorded output masks matching echoes. User cancellation and the configured tool time limit return cancelled. Never ask for the secret via another tool or copy it into a command.

Filters and textconv never run in any configuration scope; affected files carry comparison_note for raw content. No index refresh, child programs or network. Missing Git or versions below 2.40 disable Git tools.

definition.model_description: Read video frames from a workspace file or an external file with an active single-file read grant for this conversation; ReadOnly is allowed. Supply exactly one of times (1 to 12 requested times in seconds, from zero up to but excluding the duration) or count (1 to 12 uniformly spaced frames). sheet=true returns one contact sheet with time labels; otherwise each frame is an image. max_side bounds the longest side of each final image, including the whole sheet: default 1024, range 64 to 2048. Each result reports requested_time and actual_time. For an image-capable model, the newest media.frames result's images accompany the next request with shown_to_model=true, alongside the latest 3 browser screenshots. A model without image input receives times and an explicit explanation that it cannot see the images. You cannot hear the audio; this tool performs no audio transcription. Unsupported codecs and decoding timeouts return an explicit error.
